The plaintiff has filed this suit initially against the defendant Nos.1 and 2 for Specific Performance of Contract, for injunction etc.,
2.
The facts in nutshell are as follows:-

The plaintiff stated that the first defendant is the absolute owner and possessor of Western portion of site No.23, assessment No.22/1C, situated at Shidedahally,
Yashwanthapura Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, presently comes under ward No.14 of the BBMP measuring East to West 20ft, North to South 30ft, totally 600sq.ft with five square building standing thereon.
This property is O.S. No. 8730/2014.
purchased by the first defendant from R.Sandya W/o.S.Govindasing on 22-07-2011.
The first defendant offered to sell the suit property to the plaintiff, the plaintiff has agreed to purchase the same for 20,00,000/-.
It was agreed by both the parties.
Therefore, on 18- 12-2013, there was an agreement entered between the plaintiff and first defendant.

The plaintiff claimed that he has paid 14,00,000/- by way of cash in presence of the witnesses and the defendant No.1 acknowledged the payment and agreed to receive balance consideration amount of  6,00,000/- at the time of execution of the sale deed.
The first defendant also agreed to complete the sale transaction within six months from 18-12-2013.
He also assured the plaintiff that the suit property is free from all encumbrances.
The plaintiff claimed that he is always ready and willing to perform his part of contract, the time fixed for performance of contract came to an end on 17-6-2014.
The plaintiff orally requested the first defendant on many occasions to execute the sale deed by receiving the balance consideration amount.

Since the first defendant was reluctant, the plaintiff got issued legal notice on 27- 10-2014, calling upon the first defendant to execute the sale deed O.S. No. 8730/2014.
within seven days.
The first defendant has purposely evaded the service of notice, it was returned as 'intimation served'.

sentences.text: The plaintiff claimed that when he obtained the encumbrance certificate, he came to know that the first defendant has availed loan from the second defendant by mortgaging all title deeds.
The plaintiff realized that the first defendant not ready to conclude the sale deed.
Therefore, he filed suit for Specific Performance of Contract and in the alternative, sought to refund the earnest money.
He sought to decree the suit.
3. Suit summons issued to the defendant No.1.
During the pendency of this suit, suit against defendant No.2 came to be dismissed.
The first defendant filed written statement denying the contents of the plaint in toto.
He contended that there was no any agreement took place between him and the plaintiff.
The agreement of sale produced by the plaintiff is unregistered, concocted and forged.
He stated that he never intended to sell the suit property.
In para No.19 of the written statement, the first defendant stated that in the year 2013, he was running money lending business O.S. No. 8730/2014.
in the name and style of Revanth Enterprises.
The business was running very good, the other money lenders are jealous to the improvement of he first defendant.

In the second week of November 2014,
the defendant No.1 closed his shop and went to Dharmastala to take nature treatment for one month.

Taking undue advantage of the business of defendant, the other money lenders spread rumours in the society that the first defendant cheated the peoples by taking away crores of rupees to the depositors and went away.
All the people gathered in front of shop of first defendant, they vandalized the shop and took away the belongings.
It was seen by the first defendant while was returning to Bengaluru in a TV news.
He shocked and surprised to know the false news propagated by his well wishers.
He immediately contacted his lawyer and he came to know that a case was registered in Crime No.234/2014 in Srirampura Police Station against him under Section 420 of IPC.
He immediately surrendered before the 7th ACMM Court, Bengaluru and the Court has granted bail to him.
Because of commotion created, he was in a depression and his health was deteriorated.
He took some times to overcome from the incident.
After few month, he went near a shop, the shop owner sold all furniture, computers and other O.S. No. 8730/2014.
belongings of the first defendant.
He was also refused to return security deposit.
The first defendant was under duress and he was starving on many occasion with great difficulty he used to get one time mean in a day.
After the struggle, he should able to get loan from the defendant No.2 for construction of house in the suit property.
Out of loan given by the defendant No.2 he constructed the house and inducted as tenants but he could not able to pay the EMI to the Bank and became defaulter.
During this struggling period, the plaintiff and others have forged the signature of the first defendant and created the documents.
The first defendant took contention that numerous persons have filed false suit, criminal cases against him.
He narrated few instances that one P.Sridhar and others have filed O.S.No.484/2015 before CCH-48 for recovery of money.
The Court has passed attachment of property before Judgment.
He is prosecuting the case, similarly C.D.Jayanna has filed O.S.No.890/2015 for Specific Performance of Contract.

Some of the peoples have filed criminal Ravikumar M vs Kumaraswamy V on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34610298/

My findings to the above issues are as follows:-

 REASONS 8. Issue Nos.1 to 3:-
Since all these issues are revolving around the execution of agreement of sale and readiness and willingness of the parties.
Therefore, in order to avoid repeated discussion, these issues are taken together for discussion.
The case of the defendant is total denial, he denied the execution of he agreement of sale.

Therefore,
the initial burden is on the plaintiff to prove the due execution of Ex.P.1.
In order to prove the execution of Ex.P.1, he has produced the primary document i.e., agreement of sale which is marked as Ex.P.6 and examined P.W.2 to prove the execution.
Ex.P.6 is the agreement of sale executed by the first defendant in favour of the p, wherein, he stated that he intended to sell the suit property for total consideration of 20,00,000/-.
He is going to sell suit property for discharge of loan and for legal and family necessities.
As per this document on the date of execution of agreement of sale, the first defendant has received  4,00,000/- as advance amount and agreed to execute sale deed within six month.

The passing of consideration is clearly mentioned in the agreement of sale and the evidence of P.W.2 clearly goes to show that he saw the first defendant putting his signature and thumb impression on Ex.P.6.It

fulfills the requirements of due attestation and proof of Ex.P.6.
9.
He was cross-examined by the learned counsel for the first defendant nothing helpful to the case of the defendant No.1 extracted during the cross-examination of P.W.2.

The main O.S. No.
8730/2014.
objection raised by the first defendant is that in the month of November 2014, a shop was vandalized.
In the written statement he took contention that he has not entered into any agreement of sale with the plaintiff or other persons.
While the first defendant was in police custody, with the help of police, the plaintiff and other persons have obtained his signature on blank papers.

His version is completely different while cross-examining the P.Ws.1 and 2.
10.
In the cross-examination of P.WS.1, at page No.14, the first defendant suggested to him that the Agreement was forged by forged signature and thumb impression of first defendant.
The same suggestion was reflected in page No.15 of the cross-examination of P.W.1.
He took contention that on 18-12-2013, he was in the judicial custody and was behind bars in Central Prison, Bengaluru.
Therefore, on that day, he could not execute the agreement of sale in favour of the plaintiff.
This contention was not taken in the written statement nor the first defendant produced any documents to show that on the date of execution of agreement of sale he was in jail.
His version is also changing from stage to stage in the suit.

sentences.text: In the chief examination, the first defendant stated that his signature was obtained while he was in the police custody, whereas, in page No.14 of the cross-examination, the D.W.1 stated that the Agreement dated 18-12-2013 was stolen by somebody from his shop.
He says that he obtained stamp paper on 18-12-2013 signed by him and kept blank in the shop.
This is completely different story and new theory was put forth by D.W.1.

It is against to the human conduct that a person who is money lender by his profession cannot keep the blank signed stamp papers in his office that too by signing the thumb impression belonging to him.
Again, he denied his signature appearing in Ex.P.6.

In the written statement of first defendant he took specific contention in para Nos.22 and 23 that the signature of him on Ex.P.6 are forged one and it can be sent to FSL for obtaining the opinion of the expert.
He has not take any print to send is admitted disputed signature on Ex.P.6 to Forensic Lab to test the veracity of Ex.P.6.
The initial burden of proving the execution of agreement of sale is discharged by the plaintiff by examining P.W.2.
Now, onus shifts on the first defendant to prove that the signatures appearing on Ex.P.6 is not belonging to him.

Apart from it, there is a admission in the page No.40 of his cross-examination that he kept a O.S. No. 8730/2014.
signed blank paper in the office on 18-12-2013.

The important and material evidences are not produced by the first defendant firstly, he fails to prove that on 18-12-2013 he was in judicial custody in Central Jain and Ex.P.6 is not executed by him.
He produced Exs.D.1 to D.13 which are the certified copies of the suits filed by various persons.

It does not helpful for the first defendant to contended that C.D.Jayanna, P.Sridhara and others have forged his signatures and filed false suits,
criminal complaints against the defendant No.1.

From the documents produced by both the parties,
it can be safely inferred that the first defendant agreed to sell the suit property for 20,00,000/-, he received 14,00,000/- from the plaintiff as earnest money.
12. Another contention taken by the first defendant is that 14,00,000/- was paid in cash as stated n Ex.P.6.

However, it is prohibited by law i.e. Income tax Act to pay the amount exceeding 20,000/-
in cash.
It is a violation of Section 288 of Income Tax Act, for violation, there is a separate penal action which has to be initiated by the Department of Income Tax.

It does not take away the fact that consideration is passed through Ex.P.6.
O.S. No. 8730/2014.
13.
Regarding readiness and willingness, the plaintiff has produced Ex.P.1, it is a legal notice issued by the plaintiff to first defendant, it was returned as intimation served.
Filing of the suit by the plaintiff is within limitation clearly goes to show that the plaintiff is always ready and willing to perform his part of contract.
The suit filed by the plaintiff is within the limitation.
The purpose of contract is not possible because the first defendant has mortgaged the suit property to the second defendant against whom the suit is dismissed.
The first defendant is also defaulter to the second defendant - Bank.
But, the entire evidence leads me to draw inference that the pas is ready and willing to perform his part of contract.
Hence, I answer issue Nos.1 to 3 in affirmative.
14. Issue No.4:-
The first defendant has took casual contention in the written statement that the Court fee paid by the plaintiff is insufficient.

The consideration amount mentioned in the agreement of sale 20,00,000/-, the plaintiff has paid 1,09,625/- as ad volarem Court fee, which is just and Ravikumar M vs Kumaraswamy V on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34610298/
6 proper.

sentences.text: Hence, I answer issue No.4 in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.5:-

Since the plaintiff is not entitled for specific performance of contract because of the mortgage of the property in favour of the second defendant against whom the suit is dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 14-11-2014.
Therefore, refund of earnest money is the proper remedy.
Accordingly, I answer point No.5 partly in the affirmative.

16. Issue No.6:- In view of the findings on the above issues, I pass the following:-
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff partly decreed with costs.
Specific Performance of the Contract dated 18-12-2013 is refused.
However, alternative relief of refund of earnest money of 14,00,000/- is decreed.
The first defendant is directed to refund 14,00,000/- to the plaintiff within three months, failing which, the plaintiff is entitled to execute the decree.
Draw decree accordingly.
